page.layout: One page of verse, one column, with headings in italic set between the epigrams; running head at top; page number top right; signature "H j" at the lower right of the text.

main_text.l: Inferius linguam, vinclo septoque reinctam,
Vnam dum multo confpicis esse datam:
Pauca loquenda tibi, caute tardeque putato:
Sic capiti veniet gloria magna tuo.
Quae ventosa tumet Caprificus inutilis, exit
Degener e trunco Chia marisca tuo.
Haereseon fibrae veniunt a stipite sancto,
Quas fert, heu! sanctus non bene cultus ager.
Toxica quod, vitae contraria, vincere possim,
Pharmakon nomen mi Schola docta dedit,
Inventu facilis, magni non aestimor: etsi
Vis superans gemmas sit pretiosa mihi.
Ne mirare viros clara virtute micantes,
Despectos vili saepe iacere loco.

l.i: In Christo baptizatis nil nocet Satan.

main_text.l: Qui solitus diram terris aspergere pestem
Scorpius, in liquidis nil nocet ater aquis.
Vivifica Christi lotus si mergeris unda,
Nil oberunt Satanae dira venena trucis.

l.i: Lux piorum est aeterna: contra illud

main_text.l: Soles occidere & redire possunt:
Nobis si semel occidit breuis lux,
Et nox non ita longa dormiatur.

page.notes: Printed text is partly faded and show-through is present; some words in the headings and the verse are uncertain, notably "Caprificus", "Pharmakon" (printed in Greek letters, transcribed here in Latin), and "Vincetoxicum". The Greek word in the fourth epigram line is printed in Greek and was only approximated; the running head and page number are as printed.
